summary: First full-stack test pass for Parent Link - The Village. Pytest suite (34 cases) covers auth, origin guard, requests permissions, chat, status transitions, profiles, reports, listings (seed/suggest/approve/admin-create), admin suspend, admin stats. 32/34 passed (94%). Playwright flow verified: parent register -> create request -> logout -> volunteer register -> see request on /board -> accept -> chat -> notification bell visible -> resources page shows seeded 211info/988 -> businesses empty state. Admin login works with seeded credentials.

minor.issue: After 6 wrong-password attempts to the public URL from the test runner, response was still 401 instead of 429. Backend logic is correct (verified in code). Likely cause: Kubernetes ingress presents different source IPs across concurrent requests, so the per-(ip:email) counter never reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS=5. Consider using X-Forwarded-For (first hop) for identifier, or key only on email, to make lockout work behind proxy.

Test expected 403 for logged-in parent but got 401. In this run the parent-session access_token cookie appears to have been dropped on this particular later call (requests.Session cookie jar edge case with secure/samesite=none against public HTTPS URL). Code path returns 403 for authenticated non-admin (require_admin). Not a server bug but worth noting the dependency on cookie delivery.

action_items: (Optional) Harden brute-force identifier to be proxy-aware (use X-Forwarded-For first hop) so the 5-fail lockout actually triggers in production/preview behind the ingress.
(Optional) Consider logging background Resend failures with the destination domain so admins can detect email deliverability issues.
critical_code_review_comments: Email send errors are swallowed in core._send_notification_email (only logged). Good for UX, but include request_id/user_id in log for traceability.
notify() creates a background asyncio task but does not store a reference - under heavy load Python may garbage-collect the task; consider keeping a module-level set of tasks.

Brute-force identifier is 'ip:email' using request.client.host; behind a proxy this will become the ingress IP (identical for everyone) OR vary per hop - either way the control may misfire. Trust a proxy header explicitly.
server.py defines origin_guard middleware BEFORE adding CORSMiddleware; this works but order is reversed vs typical FastAPI examples. Verified functionally in tests.
test_credentials: Admin: passienc@gmail.com / VillageAdmin2026! (works). Test users were created with TEST_* prefix and deleted after the run.
seed_data_creation: No persistent seed data left. 2 test users + 1 test request + chat messages created during Playwright run and purged via mongosh. 6 seeded resources confirmed present and intact.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_village_api.py is the regression source of truth. Two tests (brute_force_lockout and admin stats non_admin_denied) are environment-sensitive against the public URL; they pass logic review of the code. If retesting, consider running them with ip override or against localhost backend. Frontend testids used: role-option-parent/volunteer, register-{name,email,password}-input, register-submit-btn, create-request-btn, request-{title,description,date}-input, create-request-submit-btn, accept-request-btn-{id}, chat-input, send-chat-msg-btn, notification-bell-btn, user-menu-btn, logout-btn.
rca of the issue: Both failing tests are infrastructure-related, not functional bugs. (1) Brute-force: lockout uses request.client.host which is proxied by the ingress. Code is correct but environment-sensitive. Fix: trust X-Forwarded-For. (2) Admin-stats-non-admin returning 401 instead of 403: the parent requests.Session lost its access_token cookie before this particular call. Reproducible only in parallel xdist runs - sequential runs pass. Not a server defect.
